metadata.rules_text:
- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is negative or neutral (e.g., post-48+ peaks, model holds high for 3-5 days).  
- Underreact to sharp downturns in sentiment (e.g., -0.70 or -0.60) — model often fails to drop below 40–45 in such cases.  
- Mean-reversion bias: model tends to overcorrect downward after strong upward moves (e.g., 49→42, then 42→40, but true often rebounds).  
- Lagged response to sentiment: if sentiment turns negative, model doesn’t adjust within 2–3 days; true price often reacts faster.  
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts overestimate early in the window (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is volatile; later days (15–30) often underestimate.  
- Avoid “over-optimism” when sentiment is consistently negative — model tends to forecast higher than true, even if history shows downward trend.
